viewsWelcome.contents:
No toolchains were found or configured. Cogitator Lens looks for gcc, clang, rustc, python, go, zig, dotnet, and nvcc on PATH, for cl and clang-cl in Visual Studio installs, and for rustup toolchains.
[Detect Toolchains](command:coglens.DetectToolchains)
[Add Toolchain](command:coglens.AddToolchain)

No toolchains are configured, and toolchain detection is turned off.
[Add Toolchain](command:coglens.AddToolchain)
[Turn On Detection](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22coglens.detectToolchainsOnPath%22%5D)

No compilation databases or CMake projects were found. Files without a variant use a C/C++ configuration of their folder, or a toolchain from the Toolchains view.
[Add Variant](command:coglens.AddCompilationVariant)
Compilation databases are read from the paths in [coglens.compilationDatabases](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22coglens.compilationDatabases%22%5D).

commands.title: Save Current Options as Artifact Preset

coglens.compilationDatabases.description: Compilation database paths resolved relative to each workspace folder. Use an empty array to disable compilation database discovery.

coglens.cppToolsConfiguration.description: Read the configurations of the C/C++ extension in .vscode/c_cpp_properties.json, and the C_Cpp.default settings. A source that no compilation database or CMake project describes gets a variant for each configuration, with its compiler, include paths, defines, and language standards. The compilation database of a configuration gives the variants of its sources.

coglens.detectToolchainsOnPath.description: Look for gcc, clang, rustc, python, go, zig, dotnet, and nvcc on PATH, also versioned compilers such as gcc-14 and clang-18. On Windows, also look for cl and clang-cl in each Visual Studio install. Also look for the rustup toolchains. Use the toolchains for files that have no other compilation variant.

coglens.processTimeout.description: Seconds that a compiler or tool may run before it is stopped.

coglens.processOutputLimit.description: Megabytes of output that a compiler or tool may write before it is stopped. A larger limit keeps more output in memory.

coglens.listingLineLimit.description: Lines that a binary disassembly or LLVM IR listing shows. A longer listing stops at this limit, and its last line says that it was truncated.

coglens.dimUnusedSourceLines.description: Dim lines that do not contribute to the rendered artifact

coglens.synchronizeSourceAndArtifactScro.description: Keep visible source and artifact editors aligned while scrolling

coglens.showAnalysisOnSource.description: Show the optimization remarks and the stack usage of open artifacts at the end of the source lines.

coglens.optimizationRemarkCategories.description: The optimization remark categories that the artifact and the source editors show.

coglens.functionCodeLens.description: Show the instruction count of each function above it in the source. The count comes from open artifacts, so it never starts a compile.

target.description: The target triple of the compiler, such as aarch64-linux-gnu. It selects the instruction documentation of assembly listings. Without it, the compiler reports its target, and a --target argument of a variant applies first.

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Cogitator Lens
walkthroughs.description: Compile a source file, and look at what the compiler makes from it.

steps.title: Find a toolchain
steps.description:
Cogitator Lens finds compilers and interpreters on PATH, in Visual Studio installs, and in rustup. You can also add one by its path.
[Detect Toolchains](command:coglens.DetectToolchains)
[Add Toolchain](command:coglens.AddToolchain)

steps.title: Open the assembly of a file
steps.description:
Open a source file, such as a C++ or Rust file. Then open its assembly beside it.
[Open Artifact](command:coglens.OpenArtifact)

steps.title: Compare two builds
steps.description:
Compare the output of two variants or two presets in a diff editor.
[Compare Artifacts](command:coglens.CompareArtifacts)

steps.title: Save options as a preset
steps.description:
A preset keeps the extra arguments and the options of one artifact kind. Open an artifact first.
[Save Current Options as Preset](command:coglens.SaveArtifactOptionsAsPreset)

scripts.compile: npm run manifest:check && npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js
scripts.package: npm run manifest:check && npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js --production
scripts.pretest: npm run manifest:check && npm run compile-tests && npm run compile && npm run lint
scripts.test:extension: npm run compile-tests && npm run compile && node scripts/run-extension-tests.mjs
